text: The tea video plays on Kuya Jun's phone, now stamped as a game fake. Bea gasps.
Dr. Fake AND Miracle Mike in one post? So many of you!
A cure-all again, Mike?
Ara fans out a set of pixel villain cards like a magician. Bea laughs and points at the Miracle Mike card.
So the tea won't fix my blood pressure?
Keep your meds as your doctor said, Lola. We'll check your BP regularly.
Kuya Jun sits beside Lola Nena and wraps a blood pressure cuff around her arm. She listens closely.
Next time, I'll ask who really said it.
You are the best, Lola Detective!
Lola Nena and Bea walk home arm in arm down the barangay street at sunset.
Kindly, Tita
Bea replies kindly in the GC, and Tita Baby checks the FDA verification portal herself.
If I just say "fake news, Tita!" she'll feel bad.
Start with thanks. She shared it out of love.
Bea sits cross-legged on the sofa, phone in hand, thinking hard. Ara floats at her shoulder.
Bea replies in the family GC.
Thank you, Tita, for always looking out for Lola! I checked this one: the doctor never said it.
A close-up of the family group chat. Bea's gentle reply sits under Tita Baby's tea forward.
Tita Baby pauses before replying.
Oh no, really? But it looked so official.
In her own living room, Tita Baby reads Bea's message, hand on her cheek.
Tita searches the FDA Philippines verification portal herself. The tea is not on the list.
Not registered, and it claims to cure everything? Oh, my.
Tita Baby squints at her laptop, searching on her own. A notebook with "CHECK FIRST" written in it lies beside her.
Proud of you, Baby!
Wow, Tita! You really are the family's light. ✨
Tita Baby shows Lola Nena her new GC message: she took down the forward and asked everyone to check with Kuya Jun first. Ara sparkles.
Kuya Jun's Busy Day
An AI tool drafts translated leaflets, and Kuya Jun still does the home visit.
Monday at the health center. The home-visit list is long.
So many leaflets to translate, so little time.
Monday morning at the health center. Kuya Jun sits behind a tall stack of leaflets, sipping coffee.
Let's try the AI tool for the first draft.
AI is fast at drafts. You're the one who checks.
Kuya Jun opens a laptop. Ara floats over the screen, cheering.
It wrote "dengue mosquitoes bite only at night". Wrong! Mostly daytime.
Human in the loop, there it is! Catch it, fix it, then share.
Kuya Jun circles a sentence on the printed draft with a red pen. Ara gives a proud thumbs up.
The leaflet is in our own language now!
And I still come by to check on you myself, Lola.
At Lola Nena's gate, Kuya Jun hands her a leaflet, a bag over his shoulder for the home visit.
Kuya, who's responsible if a leaflet is wrong?
Me and the health center. Not the AI.
Bea walks beside Kuya Jun as the street lights come on. He taps the leaflet with a confident smile.
A Poster for the Barangay
Bea makes an honest health poster: labelled, with permission and credit.
Bea, can you make a poster about miracle-cure scams?
Sure! I'll use AI for the drawing.
In the barangay hall, Aling Nena points at an empty bulletin board. Bea gives an eager nod.
I could paste a real doctor's face on it... no. That's a deepfake.
That's it! No faces without consent.
Bea sits at her laptop, an AI image tool open. She shakes her head at an idea. Ara beams.
I'll label it "Made with AI" and credit Kuya Jun's photo, with his OK.
Label, consent, credit. Great job!
Bea holds up the finished poster: a pixel teapot with a red X and a small "Made with AI" label in the corner.
Thanks for asking before using my photo, Bea.
So pretty! And honest, too.
The poster hangs on the barangay hall board. Kuya Jun and Lola Nena admire it.
My customers read it while they wait for their change!
A copy of the poster is taped to the corner store window. Aling Nena laughs as Bea grins proudly.
Lights Out, Bea
Bea stays up reading debunks, learns to rest, and joins a phone-free dinner with Lola.
1 AM. One more debunk video... then another.
Just one more video. Okay, one more more.
Bea lies in bed lit only by her phone, eyes half closed. A clock on the wall says 1 AM.
Dear, your light is still on. Time to rest?
Lola! Sorry, I lost track of time.
Lola Nena peeks in through the door in her duster, holding a glass of water. Bea sits up, startled.
The feed is built to never end. But you can end it.
Autoplay off. Phone charges outside my room.
Ara points at the endless feed on the screen. Bea switches off autoplay.
The next evening: phone-free dinner.
Now I can tell you all my stories!
Lola's stories, the best feed.
The next evening, all the phones rest in a basket by the door. The family laughs around the dinner table.
A full night's sleep. My brain feels brand new!
Rest helps mood and memory. So proud of you!
Morning sunlight fills Bea's room. She stretches by the window, fresh and smiling, as Ara cheers.
A Kiosk for Lola
The new kiosk confuses Lola, so the family gives feedback, and the kiosk gets large text and voice.
The letters are so tiny. Where do I press?
At the health center, Lola Nena stands in front of a new AI kiosk covered in small English text.
It's only in English, and it has no voice.
Many visitors struggle with it, not just Lola.
Bea and Kuya Jun look at the kiosk screen. Behind them, other visitors wait in line, also confused.
If it was built without grandparents in mind, it will miss them.
Then let's give feedback!
Ara floats by the kiosk while Bea picks up a feedback form from the counter.
The family writes feedback with the health center team.
Bigger letters, a voice, and a real person nearby.
Noted, Lola! A human option always stays.
At a barangay meeting, Lola Nena reads her feedback aloud. Kuya Jun writes it on a big sheet of paper.
A few weeks later...
There! Now it talks in Tagalog, and I can read it!
Truly for everyone!
Weeks later, the kiosk shows large letters and a speaker icon. Lola Nena taps it confidently while Ara celebrates.
The Hearing
The tea seller's app leaked buyers' data. The family learns their rights, and Lola's check-up is good.
Miracle Tea Max app
Notice: some customer names, addresses and orders may have been exposed.
Oh no! I bought the tea through that app before.
Tita Baby sits on the sofa, worried, reading a notice on her phone from the tea seller's app.
Data Privacy Act basics. Educational, not legal advice.
You have rights, Tita. You can ask what data they kept, and ask them to erase it.
Really? Even me, just a customer?
Bea sits beside Tita Baby and shows her a simple list of data rights on her phone.
The barangay holds a hearing-style info session. First the company, then the National Privacy Commission.
The company that used the AI is responsible, not "the AI".
Then I'll write to them first. If they ignore me, I go to the NPC.
At a barangay info session on data rights, a banner reads "YOUR RIGHTS". Tita Baby takes notes with a determined face.
Your blood pressure is well controlled, Lola. Keep it up!
I kept my meds and asked the right people.
At Lola Nena's check-up, Kuya Jun removes the blood pressure cuff with a big smile. Lola beams.
Season 1 · The End
Next time a miracle post comes, we pause first.
When do we trust? After we check. Thank you, family! ✨
The whole family shares dinner under a warm lamp, laughing together. Ara floats above the table, sparkling.
Ara
Aling Nena
Season 1: The Miracle Tea
Tawa-tawa cures dengue.
No herb is proven to cure dengue. If you have a high fever, see a health worker early.
Tawa-tawa is a remedy passed down with love, and many families tried it while someone got better. When a child is sick, we want to do something.
Ask your health worker. Watch for dengue warning signs and go to the hospital if they appear.
Papaya leaf juice is the real cure for dengue.
Papaya leaf is not a proven dengue cure. Care means fluids and close watch by health workers.
Stories of a neighbour who drank it and recovered spread fast. Most people with dengue do recover, so the juice gets the credit.
Do not let a remedy delay a check-up. Go to the health center early and ask about warning signs.
Dengue mosquitoes only bite at night.
Aedes mosquitoes, which spread dengue, bite mostly in the daytime.
We sleep under a mosquito net at night and hear mosquitoes buzz in the dark, so night feels like the danger time.
Check DOH dengue pages or ask your barangay health worker about daytime protection.
WHO dengue fact sheet (Aedes day-biting); DOH 4S
Dengue mosquitoes breed only in dirty water.
They breed in clean standing water. Cover, clean and empty containers every week.
Dirty canals look like the obvious problem. A clean flower pot or a drum of rain water does not look dangerous at all.
Search your home for standing water this week. Ask your health worker about DOH's 4S.
WHO dengue fact sheet; DOH 4S (search and destroy breeding places)
Fogging is all we need to stop dengue.
Fogging helps only in hotspot areas. Emptying standing water every week matters most.
Fogging is loud and visible, so it feels like strong action. Cleaning containers is quiet work that nobody sees.
Ask your barangay health worker about the 4S: search, secure, seek early, support fogging only in hotspot areas.
DOH 4S strategy
Antibiotics cure colds and flu.
Colds and flu come from viruses. Antibiotics only work on bacteria. Ask a health worker first.
Someone once felt better after antibiotics, so it seemed to work. Colds often get better on their own around that time anyway.
Ask a doctor or health worker before taking any antibiotic. Use them only when prescribed.
Stop antibiotics once you feel better and save the rest.
Use antibiotics exactly as a health worker says. Misuse helps germs become resistant.
Feeling better feels like being done, and saving medicine for next time seems thrifty and smart.
